sentences.text: The genus name Macropetalichthys translates to "armor-plated fish".
This fish possessed a dorsoventrally compressed body with dorsally facing eyes, widely splayed pectoral fins often bearing horns, and armor plates decorated with linear rows of tubercles.
The original specimen used to describe the type species was destroyed in a fire in 1891.
A neotype for the type species was designated by Babcock in 2025 from the Delaware Limestone in Columbus, Ohio.
The genus Macropetalichthys was named by Norwood and Owen in 1846.
Macropetalichthys is classified within the class Placodermi.
The genus belongs to the family Macropetalichthyidae.
Woodward assigned Macropetalichthys to the order Arthrodira in 1891, while Sepkoski later placed it in the suborder Petalichthida in 2002.
Macropetalichthys lived during the Early to Middle Devonian (Emsian to Eifelian stages) in North America and Europe.
The genus existed from the Eifelian to the Givetian stages, approximately 393.47 to 382.31 million years ago.
Researchers suggest that Macropetalichthys likely had a nektobenthic lifestyle.
